item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why:]

We are evolving Microsoft Copilot to better connect the tools people rely on with the capablities they need to build, customize, and scale AI across work. Updates include a new Home experience and enhanced Office capabilities in the Copilot app; Code and Autopilot for building solutions and automating work; an enterprise-grade platform for running code; and updates to Copilot Notebooks, Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive, and Work IQ.

[Impact on your organization:]

Home in the Copilot app:

  • When users open the Copilot app, they will land in Home, which brings Chat and Cowork together on one screen. Users can switch between Chat and Cowork in the prompt box. Read more in the blog. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • As part of this update, we are making the following updates to the left navigation pane: 1) Agents & Plugins will replace the standalone Agents entry point (called Agents & Skills for some preview users) from Chat and the Customize entry point from Cowork. 2) For users with access to Cowork, Automations from Cowork will move to the Home navigation pane. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • Researcher and Analyst will no longer be pinned by default in the Copilot app navigation pane. Users can continue to access these agents from Plugins and can pin them to the navigation pane based on their preferences. Organizations that want these agents to remain pinned for their users can pre-pin them through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Chat can complete long-running, multi-step knowledge work, including drafting email, managing meetings, working in Teams, managing OneDrive and SharePoint files, finding people, and creating Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and HTML files. Sensitive actions require user approval. Users can track and manage their long-running activity from Chat in the Tasks view, accessible in the upper right of the Copilot app navigation pane. These capabilities will roll out to Frontier later this month and are available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Chat will begin surfacing Skills that are used while generating responses, giving users greater transparency into how Copilot responds. This update will begin worldwide rollout in October and is available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Code:

  • The new Code experience gives users a dedicated place in the Copilot app to create trackers, dashboards, and apps using natural language. Users can access Code by going to the Code tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Code uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • Code is rolling out to Frontier later this month.
  • To prepare: To enable Copilot Code for your tenant, admin must deploy the unified app and set the target channel to beta.

Autopilot:

  • Autopilot, previously called Scout, is an always-on personal agent in the Copilot app with persistent context, identity, and memory. Users can access Autopilot by going to the Autopilot tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Autopilot uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • We will update this message with rollout timing and admin control details when available.

Copilot app UI updates:

  • Cowork, Code, and Autopilot entry points in the Copilot app will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Users that do not have a spending policy enabled will not be able to access these capabilities; instead, they will see an in-product message after clicking on the entry points to request access or learn more.
  • A new Microsoft 365 admin center setting will let admins choose whether users without a spending policy see Request Access or Learn More. Admins can configure whether or not users can request Copilot credits to use these experiences. Admins can also choose to block requests.
  • The existing setting in the admin center used to hide usage-based experiences (“Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing”) will be removed.
  • By default, enterprise users without a spending policy will see the “request access” message. Education users will see a Learn More link and cannot request access.
  • This update will roll out to standard customers in October and deferred customers in November.
  • To prepare: Review Microsoft 365 Admin center settings for usage-based experiences and spending policy. Decide if you want users without a spending policy to receive a "Request access" or "Learn more" message.

Full Office capabilities in the Copilot app:

  • Users can use full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint creation, editing, and collaboration capabilities in the Copilot app, side by side with Copilot. Users can also access recent Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from Library in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Capabilities accessed through Chat are included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license. Capabilities accessed through Cowork use usage-based billing.
  • These capabilities are rolling out to Frontier later this month.

Copilot Managed Runtime:

  • Copilot Managed Runtime is an enterprise-grade platform for running code within the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary under IT governance. It supports apps built in Code, Cowork, Copilot Studio, and supported command-line and SDK experiences. Admins can manage these apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Read more in the blog.
  • Managed Runtime is starting to roll out now into public preview.

Copilot Notebooks updates:

  • Copilot Notebooks will add task delegation, full Office editing and collaboration, interactive report creation, audio overview updates, model selection, and an updated user experience in the Copilot app and OneNote.
  • These updates will roll out to Frontier later this month.

SharePoint and OneDrive updates:

  • We are announcing the general availability of Copilot in SharePoint. The everyday AI capabilities that have been in public preview stay included with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). New agentic capabilities and the ability to work at greater scale than was possible in preview will be available through usage-based billing (UBB) and consume Copilot Credits. We are also introducing general availability of Copilot in OneDrive, which follows the same licensing structure as SharePoint. Read more about Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive in the blog.
  • General availability begins rolling out later this month. Tenant availability may follow as rollout progresses.
  • To prepare: No action is required to continue using capabilities included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Admins can control who can access advanced SharePoint capabilities through UBB by going to Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management. Existing cost management policies may automatically include newly available services. Existing PowerShell opt-out settings for the Public Preview of Copilot in SharePoint will continue to be honored until November 1st; after that, manage availability through SharePoint site AI settings.

Business Applications in Work IQ:

  • Work IQ now includes Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Power Platform data, enabling Copilot to ground responses and tasks on business and productivity data. Read more in the blog.
  • These updates will start rolling out in public preview later this month.
  • To prepare: Admins can configure Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data sources for Copilot in the Power Platform admin center. Admins can also manage the availability of business applications in Copilot in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings, and access through the Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) under Agents > Tools.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

In addition to the guidance listed in the individual updates above:

  • A spending policy is required for users to access capabilities available through Usage-based billing. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management. Educate users about usage-based billing scenarios and how to request access through IT. Learn more about spending policy and usage-based billing in the blog and message center post titled: Evolving Copilot pricing and new FinOps capabilities for AI.
  • Monitor this post for updated availability and deployment details.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: UBB models in Chat and Word, Excel, and PowerPoint via the model selector
item.description:
Updated November 4, 2026: We have updated the rollout schedule below. Additionally, users will be able to set the reasoning effort level when using a UBB model in Chat.

[What and why]

As previously announced in MC1479276, we are rolling out usage-based billing (UBB) models to provide users access to advanced AI in Copilot. These models will be available from Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and when using Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Users will not have access to UBB models unless UBB is enabled. We plan to rollout the ability for users to request credits from their tenant admins after this initial rollout.

GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout. Previously communicated eligibility requirements for these models apply.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier (Public): Beginning early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL) with UBB enabled
  • Tenant admins responsible for enabling usage-based billing and allocating credits

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot
  • Copilot Chat
  • Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Agent 365 cost management (Microsoft 365 admin center)

What will happen

  • After rollout, users will be able to access UBB models in the Chat model selector in the Copilot app and when using Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint if UBB is enabled.
  • After the initial rollout, we plan to roll out the ability for users to request additional credits from their tenant admin.
  • Users will not have access to UBB models unless UBB is enabled.

[Action required and recommendations]

To provide users with access to UBB models:

  • Verify that users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL).
  • Enable UBB for users who should have access to the models.
  • Allocate credits to users who should have access to the models.
  • Review your organization's governance requirements, usage expectations, and anticipated credit consumption before allocating credits.
  • Communicate your organization's process for requesting additional credits when allocated credits are consumed.
  • Review the applicable Microsoft documentation for usage-based billing and credit management before deployment.

Learn more

  • Available today: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 in Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Available today: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra in Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Evolution of the Copilot pricing model | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Understanding the user subscription license (USL) and usage-based billing (UBB) | Microsoft Learn
  • Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits | Microsoft Learn
  • Manage AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing | Microsoft Learn

 

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Users can access UBB models through Copilot Chat and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. These models process user prompts and Microsoft 365 data available through Copilot according to existing permissions and configuration.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. If UBB is for a user and they are allocated credits, users will be able to select and interact with UBB models through Copilot Chat and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Does the change include an admin control and, can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins control access through usage-based billing and credit allocation. The submitted information does not specify whether access can be scoped through Entra ID group membership.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Outlook: Share Word, Excel and PowerPoint local files via the new Outlook for Windows
item.description:
Updated November 4, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

We’re adding support for sending locally stored Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files as email attachments directly through the new Outlook for Windows. This update streamlines the sharing experience and aligns with ongoing efforts to bring feature parity between classic Outlook for Windows and the new Outlook.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557675.

[When this will happen] 

  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 (previously early November 2026) and expect to complete by mid-February 2027 (previously early December 2026).
  • General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in late February 2027 (previously mid-January) and expect to complete by late March 2027 (previously mid-February).

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users working with locally stored Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files (not stored in OneDrive).
  • Organizations adopting or transitioning to the new Outlook for Windows.

What will happen

  • Users can now share local Office files as email attachments directly through the new Outlook for Windows.
  • Users will no longer need to rely on the classic Outlook for Windows to send local file attachments.
  • This feature is ON by default.
  • There is no change to existing admin controls or policies, and all existing Outlook/Exchange policies continue to apply.

[What you can do to prepare]

No admin action is required.

To prepare your organization, you may:

  • Inform help desk staff about this update to reduce support inquiries.
  • Update your internal documentation if it references classic Outlook workflows.
  • Encourage users to adopt the new Outlook for Windows if your organization is transitioning away from classic Outlook.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Classic Outlook for Windows: Upcoming visual improvements and a more consistent Outlook experience
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We’ve heard your feedback that you’d like more information about what’s changing in classic Outlook. To help end-users understand recent changes, we’re bringing back the What’s New in-app dialog. 

The dialog is designed to be nonintrusive and will appear automatically at most once per month in Production on Current Channel. Users can dismiss it at any time and reopen it later by selecting the What’s New button on the ribbon. Administrators can turn off the automated dialog and hide its ribbon button. 

For more information and configuration instructions, see What’s New in classic Outlook for Windows.

[What and why]

We’re making updates across Microsoft Outlook experiences to improve clarity and consistency across endpoints. The first updates focus on visual details such as icons, spacing, and alignment, while maintaining familiar ways of working.

These updates are part of an ongoing series of improvements across Outlook experiences and are not a replacement for the classic Outlook experience.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

  • The initial visual updates will roll out to classic Outlook Current Channel. Users may receive individual improvements at different times as the rollout progresses.
  • We will provide additional advance notice before larger changes that might affect navigation or workflows, including timing and any preparation required.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of classic Outlook for Windows Current Channel

Platforms and services

  • The initial visual updates apply to classic Outlook for Windows Current Channel.
  • We are also improving Outlook on the web, new Outlook for Windows, and Outlook for macOS to reduce unnecessary differences and make familiar capabilities easier to recognize across devices.

What will happen

  • Users will begin seeing visual refinements to familiar mail and calendar surfaces, including updates to icons, spacing, and alignment.
  • These initial updates are intended to improve clarity and consistency without changing how users perform their tasks.
  • This change does not replace the classic Outlook experience.
  • No admin configuration changes are required for these initial visual updates.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform your help desk that the appearance of some Outlook controls may change as updates roll out.
  • Inform users as appropriate.
  • Continue to direct users to Outlook’s existing feedback options to share feedback.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Private tasks now stored in your private plan in Planner
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is updating how private tasks are stored in Microsoft Planner. Beginning in December 2026, private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences will be stored in a user's own private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.

This enables richer Planner capabilities, such as labels and task history, while maintaining the same private experience. Private tasks remain visible only to the task owner and cannot be shared or assigned to others. This change aligns private task management with the Planner platform while preserving enterprise compliance and security protections.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in early December 2026 (previously November).
  • Expected completion: late December 2026 (previously November).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who create and manage private tasks in Planner and Planner-powered experiences.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Planner
  • Planner on the web
  • Planner-powered experiences
  • Microsoft To Do

What will happen:

  • New private tasks will be stored in a private Planner plan.
  • Users will continue to see existing private tasks in Planner My Tasks.
  • Private tasks remain private to the task owner.
  • Private tasks cannot be shared or assigned to others.
  • Additional Planner task capabilities, such as labels, will become available.
  • New private tasks created in Planner will no longer appear in Microsoft To Do.
  • Existing compliance and security protections continue to apply.
  • The feature is enabled automatically.
  • No administrator action is required for deployment.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required.

You may want to:

  • Inform support and help desk teams of the change.
  • Review any internal documentation that references Planner private tasks appearing in Microsoft To Do.
  • Review the Microsoft Planner service description and admin documentation.
  • Communicate the updated experience to affected users.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change store new customer data, if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. New private tasks will be stored in a user's private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Private task storage changes from Microsoft To Do to Planner for new private tasks. Existing private tasks remain visible in Planner My Tasks.
Does the change modify retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. Organizations should validate any retention, discovery, reporting, or governance processes that depend on Microsoft To Do storage.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Admins may need to account for the storage change from To Do to Planner in reporting or governance processes.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?No. This is a Planner task storage and experience update, not a generative AI capability.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Enhanced Copilot and AI controls for meetings
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is updating how administrators and meeting organizers configure AI for Teams meetings. The existing Copilot meeting policy is being replaced by two more specific policies:

  • MeetingAI - controls whether Copilot, Facilitator, Intelligent Recap, and other AI features are available in meetings.
  • TranscriptionWithMeetingAI - controls whether transcription starts automatically when meeting AI is turned on.

This gives administrators clearer, more predictable control over whether AI is available and whether it requires (or works without) transcription, including the ability to enforce Copilot off. Organizers also gain more visibility into, and in some cases control over, these settings directly from the meeting options.

Meeting options are also being updated to make AI controls easier to understand and to provide more granular control over who can enable, manage, and use AI capabilities, including a new who can manage option that replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator meeting option:

  • Who can manage AI - replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator option and determines who can turn Copilot and other AI features on or off during a meeting. If an admin turns Meeting AI off, this option is set to No one.
  • Who can use AI - provides more granular control over which meeting participants can use Copilot and other AI capabilities.
  • Start Transcription with AI - lets organizers choose whether transcription starts with AI. Administrators can also control this option through Teams admin center.
  • Intelligent Recap controls - lets organizers decide whether an Intelligent Recap is created when Copilot is turned on, including for meetings where a transcript is not created.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously early December).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously late November 2026) and expect to complete by mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Today, the Copilot policy combines whether AI is available in a meeting with whether a saved transcript is required. After this update, these behaviors are represented by two separate settings:

  • Allow AI in meetings: On / Off, but organizers can change / Off, and organizers cannot change
  • Start transcription when AI is turned on: On, but organizers can change / On, and organizers cannot change / Off

To keep the experience predictable and avoid invalid combinations: if MeetingAI is set to enforced off, transcription will also be turned off; if transcription is then turned back on, MeetingAI will no longer be enforced off.

In PowerShell, administrators will use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI instead of the existing Copilot policy. Once the new controls are enabled, the Copilot policy can no longer be updated directly - attempts will return guidance to use the new policies.

What happens to existing configurations: Microsoft will perform a one-time update mapping each existing Copilot value to the corresponding MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI values, preserving the current effective behavior for your organization. Administrators do not need to recreate their policies. Examples include:

Copilot is on and uses a saved transcript by defaultOnOn, but organizers can change
Copilot is on and a saved transcript is requiredOnOn, and organizers cannot change
Copilot is available without transcriptionOnOff

As conditions change, such as increasing wait times, queues filling quickly, or representatives going offline, conversation orchestration can automatically take actions defined in natural-language playbooks configured by administrators.

Administrators can configure playbooks for specific scenarios using guided templates. Built-in validation identifies conflicts before playbooks are published. These capabilities help organizations automate contact center processes while improving routing, continuity, and responsiveness.

item.title: [stayInformed] Increasing user exception limit to 10,000 for Standard-Deferred release preferences
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We heard your feedback that the 100-user exception limit was too small to support meaningful pilot and validation audiences, particularly in larger organizations. We previously introduced Microsoft Entra ID group support to simplify audience management. We are now increasing the exception limit from 100 to 10,000 users per tenant, giving administrators more flexibility to manage release readiness at scale.

This update lets you assign a larger audience to a release preference different from your tenant-wide selection - for example, keeping a larger validation group on Standard release while the rest of your organization uses Deferred release.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: Administrators managing Standard and Deferred release preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What is changing:

  • The maximum exception audience increases to 10,000 users per tenant, counting users assigned individually and members of assigned groups together. This is not a per-group allowance or a limit on your organization total users.
  • You can continue using Microsoft Entra ID security groups to manage exceptions. Nested groups remain unsupported.
  • If your tenant uses Deferred release, you can assign a larger group of IT staff, help desk personnel, and business representatives to Standard release to evaluate eligible updates earlier.
  • If your tenant uses Standard release, you can assign a larger audience to Deferred release when those users need additional preparation time.
  • If a customer adds a group with more than 10,000 users, they will receive a message, during addition, notifying them of the limit.
  • If they add a group that later exceeds the limit, only the first 10,000 users will be included. The Release preferences in MAC will display a message asking them to remove the users who exceed the limit.

What is not changing: This update increases audience capacity; it does not change which features are eligible for Deferred release or how the deferred period works. Deferred release continues to delay eligible major features by approximately 30 days after their rollout to Standard release begins, not after rollout completes or after an individual pilot user receives the feature.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: New accounting capabilities in Excel and Cowork
item.description:
[What and why]

New accounting capabilities in Copilot in Excel and Cowork help finance professionals complete common accounting tasks in the tools they already use. Users can reconcile accounts, prepare journal entries, analyze financial performance and variances, and prepare financial reports. Additional capabilities support budgeting, forecasting, audit, tax, compliance, and training.

Copilot prepares the work while users retain control of review, approval, and posting. Nothing is posted automatically to an ERP or system of record without approval.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on November 13, 2026, and expect to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Accountants, AP/AR specialists, controllers, and other finance professionals with a Microsoft Copilot licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Cowork

What will happen

  • Users can reconcile accounts by comparing balances and transactions, identifying discrepancies, and preparing reconciling items for review.
  • Users can draft journal entries, including accruals, reclassifications, allocations, reversals, and recurring entries, with checks for required inputs and balanced entries.
  • Users can analyze financial performance against plan, identify key drivers, and prepare financial reporting and variance analysis.
  • Additional capabilities support budgeting, forecasting, audit, tax, compliance, and training.
  • In Excel and Cowork, finance professionals can choose to capture an audit trail when they invoke an accounting capability. When selected, a record of what Copilot changed and why is created in their chat history. Audit trails are currently available in Excel and are planned for Cowork.
  • Copilot works only with content each user can access, respects existing permissions and sensitivity labels, and stays within the Microsoft 365 service boundary.
  • Nothing is posted automatically to an ERP or system of record without user approval.
  • Accounting capabilities can use connectors as separate sources, including sources used to read from or write to ERP systems. The accounting capabilities do not depend on these connectors. Third-party accounting connectors may require separate licensing or admin enablement.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action required: During Public Preview, accounting capabilities in Excel and Cowork are available to users who have a Microsoft Copilot license and are enrolled in Microsoft Copilot Frontier. Beginning with General Availability on November 13, 2026, Frontier enrollment will not be required.

To provide access during Public Preview:

  • Assign Microsoft Copilot licenses to finance users who need access.
  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings > Frontier, turn on Frontier, and choose whether to provide access to all eligible users or specific users or groups, such as your finance team.
  • Enroll your admin account in Frontier if you need to see and manage Frontier features such as Cowork in the admin center.
  • Consider notifying your finance teams about the new accounting capabilities.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra ID: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication to retire for self-service password reset (SSPR)
item.description:
[What and why]

As Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire in Microsoft Entra ID, these methods will also become unavailable for SSPR. Organizations have 50 days after the applicable sign-in retirement rollout reaches their tenant to prepare alternative recovery methods. Users may still be able to sign in but lose the ability to reset forgotten passwords. Passkeys and other sign-in methods don't automatically satisfy SSPR requirements. Admins should identify affected users and ensure they have enough eligible recovery methods to prevent disruptions and increased helpdesk requests.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We expect rollout to begin and complete in February 2027

User populationSign-in retirement rollout beginsSSPR transition ends
Users other than Global Administrators and external usersFebruary 1, 202750 days after this rollout reaches your tenant
Global Administrators and external usersJuly 1, 202750 days after this separate rollout reaches your tenant

These are phased rollout start dates, not a single SSPR cutoff for every organization. Each population's 50-day period begins when its applicable rollout reaches your tenant. 

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations with users who rely on Microsoft-provided SMS/voice to meet their password-reset verification requirements. This includes users who have another sign-in method but still depend on SMS/voice for password recovery.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID SSPR

What will happen

When the applicable sign-in retirement rollout reaches your tenant:

  • 50-day transition: Existing SMS and voice registrations remain usable for SSPR under your current recovery policy.
  • Registration changes: SMS/voice SSPR registration and refresh prompts stop, but prompts for other eligible methods continue.
  • My Sign-Ins: Users can no longer add SMS/voice methods or edit authentication phone numbers. Existing phone registrations appear disabled, even while usable for SSPR during the transition.
  • Customer-managed telephony (CYOT): Recovery through supported providers remains available.

After the 50-day transition period:

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice are no longer available as SSPR recovery options.

User's remaining eligible recovery methodsPassword-reset experience
Enough methods to meet the applicable SSPR requirementUser can continue resetting their password with those methods
Not enough methods to meet the applicable SSPR requirementUser cannot complete SSPR and is directed to contact their administrator

The applicable one/two method requirement still applies. To retain SMS/voice for recovery, your organization must configure a supported CYOT.

Microsoft will not automatically change your SSPR policy or enable Allow password change after secure sign-in for your tenant.

[Action required and recommendations]

Prepare affected users before their applicable 50-day transition period ends:

  1. Identify affected users. Find users relying on SMS/voice for SSPR, even if they have other sign-in methods registered. Use the SMS and voice retirement and migration guidance.
  2. Prepare alternative recovery methods. Ensure users have enough eligible methods to meet SSPR policy requirements without Microsoft-provided SMS/voice. Passkeys alone don't satisfy SSPR requirements. If phone recovery is needed, configure and test a supported telephony provider before the transition ends.
  3. Test and communicate. Verify password recovery works with your SSPR policies and Conditional Access settings. Inform users and helpdesk staff about deadlines, registration steps, and support options.

Recommended: Let passkey users change a forgotten password

  • Where available, administrators can enable Allow password change after secure sign-in for eligible users. Users can then sign in with their passkey and change their password in My Sign-Ins without knowing/entering their current password.

Learn more

  • SMS and voice retirement and migration guidance
  • How Microsoft Entra self-service password reset works
  • Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication

[Compliance considerations]

If your organization needs phone-based recovery for regulatory or operational reasons, plan and validate a supported customer-managed provider before the applicable SSPR cutoff.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Viva Engage: Flexible targeting of Storyline Announcements
item.description:
Updated November 2, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

We’re introducing My Team audiences and expanded targeting capabilities in Viva Engage to help leaders communicate with the employees in their organization and tailor messages to relevant teams, departments, locations, or groups. My Team provides a ready-to-use, automatically maintained audience based on the organizational hierarchy, so leaders can reach the employees who report up to them, including both direct and indirect reports. This audience helps unlock and improve leadership experiences across Viva Engage, making Storyline Announcements, audience analytics, Leadership Corner, and feed and digest distribution more relevant with less setup.

Leaders and delegates can use My Team as-is, review its membership, or further customize and save it as a reusable audience across leader communication experiences. For Storyline Announcements, they can also define recipients at the time of publish, choosing My Team, a saved audience, or a custom audience built using organizational attributes such as department, job title, or country; existing groups like M365 Groups, distribution lists, or security groups; and individual users by name. Together, My Team and flexible targeting make leader communications more relevant, scalable, and easier to manage - with a dynamic default audience and precise targeting for relevant employee groups.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 499895.

[When this will happen:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Begins mid-November 2025 and completes by mid-March 2026 (previously early February).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Begins mid-January 2027 (previously early November 2026) and completes by late February 2027 (previously late November 2026).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected: Leaders and delegates using Viva Engage Storyline Announcements in tenants enrolled in public preview.

What will happen:

  • This capability is being introduced as part of the public preview for Viva Engage. During this phase, leaders and their delegates can actively experiment with flexible audience targeting for Storyline Announcements—defining a custom audience at the time of posting, rather than relying solely on pre‑configured Leader Audiences.
  • Audiences can include organizational attributes (such as reporting structure, country, department, job title), existing groups (Microsoft 365 Groups, DLs, SGs), or individual users.
  • Notifications and delivery channels (Teams, email, Viva Engage Inbox) remain unchanged for recipients.
  • No dependency on IT or advance audience setup—leaders can act immediately when communication needs arise.
  • Available only in public preview; functionality and targeting options may evolve before general availability.
  • Admins should ensure organizational attributes in Entra ID or Organizational Data in Microsoft are accurate to support successful targeting.
  • Available platforms: Desktop and web.
  • Licensing requirements: This feature requires a premium license available through Viva or Communications and Communities (C&C). Availability may vary depending on your organization's Microsoft 365 licensing agreement.

[What you can do to prepare:]

No admin action is required for rollout. To prepare, you may want to:

  • Validate organizational attributes (reporting structure, country, department, role, job title) in Microsoft Entra ID or Organizational Data in Microsoft.
  • Confirm leader and delegate assignments to ensure the right people can use Storyline Announcements and the new targeting control.
